headline: 11-party alliance to hold Dhaka rally tomorrow on AL anniversary
summary: The Jamaat-e-Islami-led coalition demands trials for enforced disappearances and massacres committed by the banned Awami League.
details: The Jamaat-e-Islami-led 11-party alliance has announced a rally in Dhaka tomorrow, coinciding with the founding anniversary of the Awami League, whose activities remain banned.
The rally, scheduled for 5:00 PM at Bijoynagar, will demand trials for all enforced disappearances, killings, and massacres committed by the former fascist Awami League government.
Jamaat Ameer and Opposition Leader Shafiqur Rahman is expected to attend as the chief guest.
Beyond the Dhaka event, the alliance has also announced nationwide protest rallies and processions across all districts on July 4.

At a press briefing in Moghbazar, liaison committee coordinator Hamidur Rahman Azad stated that the protests are also aimed at addressing rising commodity prices and the deterioration of law and order.
Azad alleged that the country's independence and sovereignty were compromised over the last 17 years to keep the previous government in power.
He further claimed that justice remains elusive for victims of the 2009 Pilkhana tragedy, extrajudicial killings, and the July-August 2024 mass killings.
The alliance is also preparing a 36-day program to mark the second anniversary of the July Uprising, which will be finalized by June 25.
caption:
11 parties unite for a massive rally in Dhaka tomorrow to demand justice for massacres and disappearances.

The Jamaat-e-Islami-led 11-party alliance has announced a rally in Dhaka tomorrow, coinciding with the founding anniversary of the Awami League, whose activities remain banned.

The rally, scheduled for 5:00 PM at Bijoynagar, will demand trials for all enforced disappearances, killings, and massacres committed by the former fascist Awami League government.

Jamaat Ameer and Opposition Leader Shafiqur Rahman is expected to attend as the chief guest.

Beyond the Dhaka event, the alliance has also announced nationwide protest rallies and processions across all districts on July 4.

At a press briefing in Moghbazar, liaison committee coordinator Hamidur Rahman Azad stated that the protests are also aimed at addressing rising commodity prices and the deterioration of law and order.

Azad alleged that the country's independence and sovereignty were compromised over the last 17 years to keep the previous government in power.

He further claimed that justice remains elusive for victims of the 2009 Pilkhana tragedy, extrajudicial killings, and the July-August 2024 mass killings.

The alliance is also preparing a 36-day program to mark the second anniversary of the July Uprising, which will be finalized by June 25.

#Bangladesh #Dhaka #Politics #Jamaat #Justice

Source: The Daily Star, Jamuna TV, Somoy News
